snippet.title: Terremoto de magnitude 7,7 atinge o Panamá
snippet.description:
Um terremoto de magnitude 7,7, em uma escala que vai até 10, atingiu o Panamá. De acordo com o Serviço Geológico dos Estados Unidos, o epicentro foi próximo a uma área rural, no sul do país, a 12 km de profundidade. 

O abalo também foi sentido na capital, Cidade do Panamá, onde casas e carros foram danificados. Por medida de segurança, moradores e turistas deixaram os imóveis e permaneceram nas ruas. Em outra cidade, um prédio desabou. 

No Canal do Panamá, importante rota comercial, protocolos de emergência foram acionados, mas as operações continuaram normalmente. Voos foram suspensos após o terremoto. 

Tremores secundários também foram registrados. Um alerta de tsunami chegou a ser emitido, mas foi retirado pelas autoridades. Até o momento, não havia relatos de vítimas.

snippet.title: The ATF Just Dropped The Biggest NFA Surprise In Decades
snippet.description:
A couple of years ago, buying a suppressor meant fingerprints, paperwork, a federal registry, and waiting the better part of a year.

Now the ATF says you can walk into a gun store, buy one, and take it home.

No NFA permission slip.

No federal registry.

No year-long wait.

Suppressors, short-barreled rifles, short-barreled shotguns, and “any other weapons” just moved into a completely different world.

But there is a catch.

This did not happen because Congress fully repealed that part of the NFA.

It happened because the tax was dropped to zero, a Texas judge said the government cannot keep running a registry off a tax that no longer exists, and this ATF chose to apply that approach more broadly.

That choice matters.

Because the key phrase in the letter is “enforcement discretion.”

That means this ATF is choosing not to enforce it this way.

A future ATF could choose differently.

This video breaks down what the ATF open letter actually says, what changed for suppressors and SBRs, what still applies, why machine guns and destructive devices are untouched, why state law can still jam you up, why interstate travel matters, and why this win only becomes permanent if Congress locks it in.

So yes, celebrate.

Buy the can.

Build the SBR.

But know your state laws, understand the fine print, and do not confuse an agency’s choice with a permanent change in federal law.

While most people head to a café with their laptops, this artist brings a tiny watercolor kit.
And you can't believe what she can achieve with this little setup.
Instead of needing a full setup or expensive equipment, she carries everything she needs in a small kit, ready to paint wherever inspiration strikes.
But the real secret is her water brush pen, allowing her to paint without carrying a separate water cup or worrying about making a mess.
So would you say the simplicity of the tools is what makes the art feel more human?

snippet.title: CAF have confirmed that VAR will noW be used in the CAFCL and CAFCC group stages from this season.
snippet.description:
CAF confirms VAR from group stage of 2026-2027 club competitions
Another milestone in the modernisation of refereeing

Refereeing in the 2026–2027 Champions League and Confederation Cup is set to undergo a revolution.

The acting general secretary of the Confederation of African Football, Samson Adamu, has confirmed that VAR will be used from the group stage of both club competitions this season. This development marks a significant change in the system of referee assistance in African club competitions.

Until now, the technology had only been deployed from the quarter-finals of the Champions League and the Confederation Cup onwards. With this new measure, teams competing in the group stages will therefore be able to benefit from video assistance.

Teams competing in the Champions League and the Confederation Cup are preparing for the second and final qualifying round.

Samson Adamu, the acting secretary general of the Confederation of African Football, stated in media remarks that video technology will begin to appear during the group stage of both competitions, in a new step within the refereeing system of African tournaments.



Zamalek SC and Pyramids FC represent Egypt in the CAF Champions League, while Al Ahly FC and ZED compete in the CAF Confederation Cup.



In conclusion, African football fans, especially Egyptian supporters, are eagerly anticipating the positive impact of this technology on fairness in the game, amid great ambitions for the Egyptian quartet (Al Ahly FC, Zamalek SC, Pyramids FC, and Zed) to deliver strong performances and honor Egyptian football on the continental stage.
